"evil is evil" is a really dangerous perspective.
Actions have moral dimensions- your intent, the power, and most importantly necessity- like I said, survival.

Treating 2 situations differently isn't necessarily having double standards. Its hypocrisy when we apply different principles to somewhat comparable situations just cause one person is someone we like/) sympathise with.
Or when we apply the same principle to situations that are not comparable- starving man vs greedy politician.

You'd much rather have a lying politician than a lying friend..
A politician's lie affects millions of people. A friends lie is something personal that affects you alone. Or a few others impacted.
Opens a door to greater good vs personal discomfort?

If someone steals to satisfy greed, to get a 3rd home and someone steals to avoid starvation, calling both actions wrong is very much reasonable.
However callin them equally wrong is completely different na?

And perhaps the most important distinctionis that we can hold people accountable while acknowledging that everyone who breaks the same rules do not deserve the same moral judgment.

That isn't double standards or hypocrisy, I think it's nuance.
